exercise.name: Barbell Front Foot Elevated Split Squat

reference.title: Barbell Split Squat Front Foot Elevated
reference.listing: Video (title and product number from the listing URL; the page itself could not be read from this environment, so the movement follows the exercise name and standard coaching)

breathing.pattern: Inhale on the way down, exhale on the way up.
breathing.cadence: About 1.9 s down, short pause, about 1.1 s up

prescription.progression: Add 2.5 kg when every rep reaches full depth.

cues.text: Bar on the upper traps just below the bony bump at the base of the neck, hands just outside the shoulders, elbows down, shoulder blades squeezed. Put the whole right foot on a low step, the left foot back on its ball, feet hip width apart sideways.
Brace and drop the hips straight down; the front knee travels forward over the toes and the chest stays up under the bar.
Lower the back knee to just above the floor, below the level of the front foot; front heel stays down.
Drive through the front foot to stand back up; breathe out as you rise.
Stand tall in the split stance, re-brace, repeat, then switch legs.

mistakes.mistake: Stance too short, so the front heel lifts
mistakes.fix: Set the back foot about one leg length behind the step.
Most of the weight stays on the front foot; the back leg only balances.
Keep the knee over the middle toes.
Keep the chest up and the bar over the middle of the stance.

kinematics.norm: A low step or plate, about 5-15 cm (common coaching; clinical opinion)
About one leg length was suggested as optimal in the split squat (Song 2023)
More than in a flat split squat; about 100-110 degrees at the bottom (clinical opinion)
Drops toward the floor, below the front foot (clinical opinion)
About 2 s down, 1 s up (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual, Barbell Split Squat Front Foot Elevated, video (movement reference only)
Song et al. 2023, effects of step lengths on lower-extremity biomechanics during the split squat (Front Bioeng Biotechnol 11:1277493)
Mausehund, Skard & Krosshaug 2019, muscle activation in unilateral barbell exercises: implications for strength training and rehabilitation (J Strength Cond Res 33(7S):S85-S94)
Hip-muscle activation during the lunge, single-leg squat, and step-up-and-over exercises (J Sport Rehabil 18(1):91-103, 2009; PubMed 19321909)

cautions: Unrack the bar from a squat rack (J-hooks at about mid-chest height) and re-rack it after the set; set the safeties or use a spotter.
Keep the bar on the muscle of the upper back, never on the neck.
Set the step so it cannot slide.
The deficit takes the back knee very low: build depth over several sessions.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness, tingling or giving-way occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Lower step or none while learning.

muscleNotes.quads_r: Front-leg knee extensors; raising the front foot lets the front knee and hip bend further than in a flat split squat (clinical opinion). Split squat vastus lateralis activity was similar to the Bulgarian split squat (Mausehund 2019).
muscleNotes.quads_l: Front-leg knee extensors; raising the front foot lets the front knee and hip bend further than in a flat split squat (clinical opinion). Split squat vastus lateralis activity was similar to the Bulgarian split squat (Mausehund 2019).
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Front-leg hip extensor, stretched further at the bottom of the deeper range (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Front-leg hip extensor, stretched further at the bottom of the deeper range (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.adductors_r: Adductor magnus assists hip extension in the deep front-hip position (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.adductors_l: Adductor magnus assists hip extension in the deep front-hip position (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Assist hip extension on the front leg (Mausehund 2019 measured biceps femoris in the split squat).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_l: Assist hip extension on the front leg (Mausehund 2019 measured biceps femoris in the split squat).
muscleNotes.calves_r: Steady the front shin on the step; the back calf holds the heel up.
muscleNotes.calves_l: Steady the front shin on the step; the back calf holds the heel up.
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Holds the pelvis level on the narrow base (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Holds the pelvis level on the narrow base (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the trunk tall and the pelvis square.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Hold the trunk upright as it tips slightly forward.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Hold the trunk upright as it tips slightly forward.
muscleNotes.hip_flexors_r: The back-leg hip flexors lengthen as the back knee drops below the front foot (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.hip_flexors_l: The back-leg hip flexors lengthen as the back knee drops below the front foot (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: The muscle shelf the bar rests on.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_l: The muscle shelf the bar rests on.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Squeeze the shoulder blades together so the upper back forms a tight shelf.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_l: Squeeze the shoulder blades together so the upper back forms a tight shelf.
muscleNotes.lats_r: Pull the bar down into the back and keep the upper back tight.
muscleNotes.lats_l: Pull the bar down into the back and keep the upper back tight.
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_r: Grip the bar to hold it in place on the back.
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_l: Grip the bar to hold it in place on the back.
